messages:
Carla: Quick sync — for the next Dedicated launch we need unambiguous acceptance criteria around committed capacity: guaranteed headroom, smoothing window behavior, and a clear fallback path. Who can own a short checklist?

Ben: I can take a first pass. Question: do we standardize on per-tenant smoothing or an org-wide soft cap?

Derek: Per-tenant smoothing + a global emergency cap. Otherwise noisy tenants will monopolize warm replicas. Implement with a token-bucket per tenant, refill tied to commit tier.

Elaine: +1. Also we need to call out SLA deltas: e.g., pinned capacity 99.95 latency SLO, elastic fallback 99.5 — customers must understand tradeoffs. Product needs to sign off.

Carla: Agreed. Minimal checklist items I want: 1) preemption/muting behavior defined and exercised, 2) observability hooks (per-route p95/p99, token usage), 3) billing reconciliation for smoothing credits, 4) contract toggle for hard vs. soft commit.

Ben: Draft checklist below — feedback welcome.

```yaml
# acceptance_checklist: dedicated-commit
- load_tests: sustained 5k qps for canary tenants OR 90th percentile burst profile satisfied
- sla_telemetry: p95/p99, error_rate, cold_start_rate, cache_hit_ratio
- autoscale_policy: predictive_prewarm: true
  smoothing_window_sec: 300
  guaranteed_replicas: 2
  emergency_fallback_variant: low_mem_quant
- billing: smoothing_credits_accounted, invoice_preview
- contract: smoothing_opt_in_flag
```

Derek: One tweak: rename min_replicas -> guaranteed_replicas in the config above. Also specify eviction_grace_sec so sessions don't break on preempt.

Elaine: Do we make smoothing opt-in by default? Some enterprise customers demand hard reserved lanes. Proposal: default to soft (opt-out for hard reserve in contract).

Ben: Noted. For launch gating I suggest: canary with 3 customers representing different traffic shapes (steady, spiky, chatty). If that passes, open to broader rollout.

InfraBot: Heads-up: rollout will require short-lived 2x capacity staging for blue/green switch; estimate 48h of extra provisioning during canary. Also rolling updates must preserve token buckets, otherwise smoothing semantics break.

Carla: Good catch. Add to checklist: migration procedure + runbook for rollback.

Derek: On autoscale policy decision: leaning toward predictive pre-warm (ML-backed) + deterministic 5-min smoothing ramp, with immediate fallback to a lighter quantized variant when capacity constrained. That keeps latency stable.

Elaine: Action items: Ben to post full doc today, Derek to add tracing and eviction specifics, Infra to give cost estimate and staging window. We'll gate launch on: load tests pass, SLO telemetry stable, billing preview validated, and legal signoff on opt-in toggle.

Ben: I'll post the doc in #product and link load test results. @Derek @InfraBot tagging you for inputs.

Carla: Thanks team. :thumbsup: We'll slot this for Monday product sync to finalize launch date.

Ben: quick example PromQL for the telemetry dashboard: `rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="dedicated"}[5m])` — we'll need a derived panel for token consumption per-tenant.

Derek: I'll add a trace span for "smoothing_token.acquire" so we can break down latency impact.

InfraBot: Cost estimate request received — returning ETA: 24h.

Carla: Perfect. Closing loop here — expect the checklist doc by EOD and we'll review in sync.
